Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-492", "title": "Eye Injuries", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "The structure of your face helps protect your eyes from injury."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Still, injuries can damage your eye, sometimes severely enough that you could lose your vision."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "If you play sports or work in certain jobs, you may need protection."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The most common type of injury happens when something irritates the outer surface of your eye."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Certain jobs such as industrial jobs or hobbies such as carpentry make this type of injury more likely."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It's also more likely if you wear contact lenses."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "With chemicals, the pain may cause you to close your eyes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "This traps the irritant next to the eye and may cause more damage."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You should wash out your eye right away while you wait for medical help."}]}, {"id": "MLP-118", "title": "Erectile Dysfunction", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Erectile dysfunction (ED) is a common type of male sexual dysfunction."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is when a man has trouble getting or keeping an erection."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "ED becomes more common as you get older."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Some people have trouble speaking with their doctors about sex."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But if you have ED, you should tell your doctor."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It may mean your blood vessels are clogged."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It may mean you have nerve damage from diabetes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If you don't see your doctor, these problems will go untreated."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Your doctor can offer several new treatments for ED."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "For many men, the answer is as simple as taking a pill."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Getting more exercise, losing weight, or stopping smoking may also help."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5955", "title": "Aplastic Anemia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Aplastic anemia is a rare but serious blood disorder."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "If you have it, your bone marrow doesn't make enough new blood cells."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It happens when there is damage to stem cells inside your bone marrow."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are different types of aplastic anemia, including Fanconi anemia."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The causes of aplastic anemia can include: Autoimmune disorders , which are the most common cause Certain inherited gene changes, such as the one that can cause Fanconi anemia Toxic substances, such as pesticides , arsenic , and benzene Radiation therapy and chemotherapy for cancer Certain medicines Viral infections such as hepatitis , Epstein-Barr virus, or HIV Pregnancy In many people, the cause is unknown."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This is called idiopathic aplastic anemia."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "What are the symptoms of aplastic anemia?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Aplastic anemia can develop suddenly or slowly."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The symptoms of aplastic anemia can include: Fatigue Weakness Dizziness Shortness of breath Easy bruising or bleeding What other problems can aplastic anemia cause?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Aplastic anemia can cause other problems, including frequent infections and bleeding."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It raises your risk of developing a serious blood disorder ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If not treated, aplastic anemia can also lead to heart problems such as an arrhythmia (a problem with the rate or rhythm of your heartbeat), an enlarged heart, or heart failure ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "To find out if you have aplastic anemia, your doctor will: Take your medical and your family medical histories Do a physical exam Order tests, such as tests to check if you have low numbers of cells in your bone marrow and blood What are the treatments for aplastic anemia?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If you have aplastic anemia, your doctor will create a treatment plan for you."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The plan will be based on how severe the anemia is and what is causing it."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Treatments can include: Blood transfusions Blood and marrow stem cell transplants Medicines to suppress your immune system Because of the risk of blood disorders, your doctor will monitor your condition and screen you for blood disorders regularly."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6521", "title": "Reflux in Children", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Gastroesophageal reflux (GER), often called reflux, occurs when food or stomach acid flows back from your child's stomach into the esophagus."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The esophagus is the tube that carries food from your mouth to your stomach."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This can sometimes cause irritation or a burning sensation."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Occasional reflux is common and usually not a problem."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Gastroesophageal reflux disease ( GERD ) is a more serious and long-lasting type of reflux."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "GERD can cause repeated symptoms or damage to the lining of the esophagus."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Having reflux two or more times a week may be a sign of GERD."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your child's health care provider may diagnose GERD if the reflux causes pain, feeding problems, or irritation of the esophagus."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What causes reflux and GERD in children?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "A small muscle called the lower esophageal sphincter acts as a valve between the esophagus and stomach."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "When your child swallows, this muscle relaxes to let food pass from the esophagus to the stomach."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "This muscle normally stays closed, so the stomach contents and acid don't flow back into the esophagus."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "This muscle, along with the diaphragm (the large muscle between the chest and abdomen), usually prevents reflux."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It's normal for children to have reflux occasionally."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "In children who have GERD, the lower esophageal sphincter may be weak or relax when it shouldn't."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "That allows stomach contents into the esophagus."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "This can happen because of: A hiatal hernia , a condition in which the upper part of the stomach pushes up into the chest Increased pressure on the abdomen (belly) from being overweight or having obesity Certain medicines, such as some used to treat asthma , allergies , depression , or pain Smoking or exposure to secondhand smoke Previous surgery on the esophagus or upper abdomen Developmental delays or certain neurological conditions , such as cerebral palsy Lung conditions, such as cystic fibrosis How common are reflux and GERD in children?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Many children have occasional reflux, especially after large meals or physical activity."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "GERD is less common, and most symptoms improve with time and lifestyle changes."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "What are the symptoms of reflux and GERD in children?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Some children might not even notice reflux, while others may taste food or stomach acid in the back of their mouth."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "In children, GERD can cause: Heartburn , a burning feeling in the chest or throat (more common in older children and teens) Bad breath Nausea or vomiting Trouble or pain when swallowing Cough , hoarseness, or breathing problems Wearing away of tooth enamel from stomach acid Other conditions can cause similar symptoms."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Talk to your child's provider if symptoms happen often or make eating, sleeping, or daily activities difficult."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "How are reflux and GERD diagnosed in children?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "In most cases, your child's provider can tell if it's reflux by learning about your child's symptoms and health history."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Tests are usually needed only if symptoms don't get better with lifestyle changes or medicines, or if another health problem is suspected."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Common tests include: Upper GI series , which looks at the shape of your child's upper GI (gastrointestinal) tract."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Your child will drink or eat a chalky-tasting liquid called barium."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "For young children, the barium is mixed in with a bottle or other food."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Several x-rays are taken to track the barium as it goes through your child's esophagus and stomach."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Esophageal pH and impedance monitoring , which measures the amount of acid or liquid in your child's esophagus."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "A thin flexible tube is placed through their nose into the stomach."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The end of the tube in the esophagus measures when and how much acid comes up into the esophagus."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "The other end of the tube attaches to a monitor that records the measurements."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Your child will wear the tube for 24 hours."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "They may need to stay in the hospital during the test."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Upper gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy and biopsy , which uses an endoscope, a long, flexible tube with a light and camera at the end of it."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "An endoscope is inserted down your child's esophagus, stomach, and first part of the small intestine."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "While looking at the pictures from the endoscope, tissue samples (biopsy) may be taken."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "What lifestyle changes can help treat my child's reflux or GERD?"}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Simple lifestyle changes can often improve symptoms."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Examples include: Maintaining a healthy weight."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Avoiding high-fat foods or other trigger foods that cause symptoms."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Wearing loose-fitting clothing around the abdomen (belly)."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Staying upright for 3 hours after meals and avoiding slouching when sitting."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Sleeping with the head of the bed raised 6 to 8 inches."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "What are the treatments for my child's GERD?"}, {"id": "S047", "text": "If lifestyle changes aren't enough, your provider may recommend medicine to reduce stomach acid."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "The medicines work by lowering the amount of acid your child's stomach makes."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Some are available over-the-counter , while others need a prescription."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Do not give your child any medicine unless your provider recommends it."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "If symptoms don't get better or are severe, your provider may refer you to a doctor who treats stomach and digestion problems in children."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "In rare cases, surgery may be considered."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "If GERD isn't treated, it can cause problems such as inflammation or scarring in the esophagus, changes in its lining (Barrett's esophagus), or make breathing problems, like asthma, worse."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-514", "title": "Intimate Partner Violence", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What is intimate partner violence (IPV)?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Intimate partner violence (IPV) is abuse that happens in a romantic relationship."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The intimate partner could be a current or former spouse or dating partner."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "IPV can happen one time, or it may be ongoing."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It may include different types of abuse, such as: Physical violence , which is when a person hurts or tries to hurt a partner by hitting, kicking, or using another type of physical force."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Sexual violence which involves forcing or attempting to force a partner to take part in sexual activity when the partner does not or cannot consent."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The sexual activity could include things like sex acts, sexual touching, or non-physical sexual events (e.g., sexting)."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Emotional abuse , which includes threats, name-calling, put-downs, and humiliation."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It can also involve controlling behavior, such as telling a partner how to act or dress and not letting them see family or friends."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Economic abuse , also called financial abuse, involves controlling access to money."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Stalking , which is repeated, unwanted contact that causes fear or concern for the safety of the partner."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "This can include watching or following the partner."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The stalker may send repeated, unwanted phone calls or texts."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Who is affected by intimate partner violence (IPV)?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "It is hard to know exactly how common IPV is because it is often not reported."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "But we do know that IPV can happen to anyone."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "It affects people with all levels of income and education."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What are the signs that someone is experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV)?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "If you think that a loved one might be experiencing IPV, watch for these signs: Does your friend or loved one: Have unexplained cuts or bruises?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Avoid friends, family, and favorite activities?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Make excuses for their partner's behavior?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Look uncomfortable or fearful around their partner?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Does your friend or loved one's partner: Yell at or make fun of them?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Try to control them by making all the decisions?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Force them to do sexual things they don't want to do?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Threaten to hurt themself if the partner wants to break up?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "What can I do if I am experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV)?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Your safety is the most important concern."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If you are in immediate danger, call 911."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "If you are not in immediate danger, you can: Get medical care if you have been injured or sexually assaulted."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Call a helpline for free, anonymous help."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "You can contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-799-SAFE (7233) or 800-787-3224 (TTY)."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "You can also chat with them through their website or through text by texting START to 88788."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Find out where to get help in your community."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Contact local organizations that can help you."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Intimate partner violence usually does not get better."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Think about a safe place for you to go and all the things you will need when you leave."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Keep evidence of abuse, such as pictures of your injuries or threatening emails or texts."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Make sure that it is in a safe place the abuser cannot access."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Talk to someone you trust , such as a family member, a friend, a co-worker, or a spiritual leader."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Consider getting a restraining order to protect yourself."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "How can I help someone who is experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV)?"}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Let your loved one know that being treated this way isn't healthy and that they are not to blame."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "You should: Call 911 if there is immediate danger."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Learn about the signs and keep track of the ones that you see."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Get the addresses and phone numbers of some local resources in your community."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Then, you'll be able to share the information if the person is ready for it."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Make sure you can have your conversation in a safe, private place."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Your loved one's partner may have access to their cell phone or computer, so be careful about sharing information over text or email."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Describe the behaviors that concern you."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Be as specific as possible when explaining why you are worried."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "If your loved one is ready to leave an abusive partner, help them make a plan for getting out of the relationship as safely as possible."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "An intimate partner violence counselor can help with making a safety plan."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "You should talk about your concerns with your loved one, but you need to understand that they may not be ready to talk about it."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "Let them know that you're available to talk at any time, and that you will listen without judging them."}]}]
